subject.title: Feature: configurable LLM retry with backoff on transient errors (overloaded/529)

question: Should OpenClaw add a public openclaw.json LLM retry/backoff contract for model providers, and if so should it be provider-level, agent-level, or limited to the existing session/provider SDK retry settings?
rationale: The requested behavior crosses public config schema, provider SDK retry behavior, embedded-agent failover semantics, and idempotency/availability tradeoffs, so automation should not invent the permanent API shape.

options.title: Approve a provider-level retry contract
options.body: Define models.providers.<id>.retry as the canonical public config surface and require runtime wiring, docs, upgrade proof, and tests before closing this issue.

options.title: Constrain retries to existing SDK settings
options.body: Document and harden retry.provider settings instead of adding a new openclaw.json provider schema, then close this issue as intentionally out of scope for core config.

options.title: Defer configurable retries
options.body: Keep hardcoded same-model retry and failover behavior only, leaving configurable transient retry policy unplanned until a narrower provider incident proves the need.

recommendation.title: Approve a provider-level retry contract
recommendation.body: Define models.providers.<id>.retry as the canonical public config surface and require runtime wiring, docs, upgrade proof, and tests before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision most directly affects agent/failover runtime semantics that this account recently changed and gated for idempotency.
